key_insight: The paper argues that medical AI should move beyond static diagnosis toward medical world models that simulate how patient states evolve and how treatments may change future outcomes.
clinical_relevance: This framework could help clinicians anticipate deterioration, compare treatment-conditioned futures, and personalize intervention planning over time.
method: Reviews and organizes related work into three linked capabilities: patient-state construction, clinical dynamics modelling, and intervention decision support.
Connects foundation models, longitudinal modelling, disease simulation, treatment-effect estimation, reinforcement learning, and digital twins into a perception–dynamics–planning roadmap.
Highlights how partial systems can be combined into more mature simulators of disease progression and treatment response.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a review of representative systems and comparison across related literature rather than reporting a new dataset or quantitative experiment.
watch_item: Plausible simulated rollouts may not be clinically reliable without strong validation, especially when used to guide real intervention decisions.
paper_title: Medical world models: representing medical states, modelling clinical dynamics and guiding intervention policies
